hints.title: Complete Graph Minimum Spanning Tree Obstacle
hints.text: Connecting n 2D points with minimal total Manhattan distance corresponds to building a minimum spanning tree on a complete graph. How can greedily expanding a connected tree one closest point at a time optimize total cost?

hints.title: Greedy Frontier Distance Relaxation Invariant
hints.text: Greedy component expansion maintains the minimum distance from the current tree to every unvisited vertex. In each step, the closest unvisited vertex is permanently added.

hints.title: Prim Minimum Distance Array Procedure
hints.text: Initialize visited flags and an array of minimum distances from the growing tree, setting the starting point distance to 0. Over n iterations, pick the unvisited point with the smallest recorded distance, add its distance to the total cost, mark it visited, and relax distances to all remaining unvisited points using Manhattan distance. Return the total accumulated cost.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Prim algorithm using a 1D min-distance array runs in O(N^2) time and optimal O(N) space on a dense graph.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Kruskal algorithm generates N * (N - 1) / 2 explicit edges taking O(N^2 log N) time and O(N^2) memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array-based Prim avoids edge allocations, fitting comfortably within O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Knowing that Prim with an array beats Kruskal or heap-based Prim on dense complete graphs.
